strings.name: Vicki Hollub
strings.role: Occidental director and former president and CEO
strings.summary: Vicki Hollub rose from engineering roles to lead Occidental as CEO from 2016 to 2026. Her tenure included the Anadarko acquisition and investment in direct air capture, alongside acquisition-related debt and investor scrutiny. She stepped down from executive leadership in June 2026 and remained a director.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026, including a September filing supporting her recent status. Her birth year has not been reliably established. Carbon capture investment and net-zero targets are distinct from verified emissions reductions.
strings.influence.rationale: Led Occidental and participated in major energy acquisitions and the commercial development of direct air capture projects.
strings.facts.f1.label: Engineering education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a Bachelor of Science in Mineral Engineering from the University of Alabama in 1981.
strings.facts.f2.label: International operations
strings.facts.f2.value: Held technical and management roles in the United States, Russia, Venezuela and Ecuador.
strings.highlights.h1.title: A woman leading a major oil company
strings.highlights.h1.text: Became the first female CEO of a major U.S. oil and gas company in 2016.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Investment in direct air capture
strings.highlights.h2.text: Promoted commercial deployment of the technology during her tenure. Buying Carbon Engineering expanded this business, but investment alone does not demonstrate net emissions reductions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Stepped down as CEO and remained a director
strings.timeline.t1.text: Richard Jackson succeeded her as president and CEO. Hollub remained on the board, and a September filing continued to identify her as a director.
strings.timeline.t2.title: CrownRock acquisition completed
strings.timeline.t2.text: Occidental announced the transaction had closed, a corporate acquisition during her tenure as CEO.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Completion of Carbon Engineering acquisition announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: An Occidental subsidiary acquired the direct air capture technology company for approximately US$1.1 billion in cash consideration, payable in installments.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Anadarko acquisition completed
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company reported a transaction value of US$55 billion including assumed debt. Reuters later reviewed the resulting pressure to reduce debt and investor scrutiny.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Occidental CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Stephen Chazen, completing the company's previously announced succession plan.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became president and chief operating officer
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became president and COO and joined the board, before succeeding to the CEO role in 2016.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Occidental
strings.timeline.t7.text: The company's 2016 regulatory filing dates the start of her employment at Occidental to 1982.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduated and began an engineering career
strings.timeline.t8.text: After earning her mineral engineering degree, she worked as an engineer at Cities Service. Her Senate testimony identifies this year as the start of her career.
